subject: Data retention exception request / FinTechCorp — follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <s.liu@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention exception request / FinTechCorp — follow-up

Hi Sarah — great speaking with you earlier. Thanks for the clear context on FinTechCorp's requirements. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of ask
- FinTechCorp requires zero retention of any raw transcripts or session logs containing PII (names, SSNs, account numbers) originating from user prompts.
- You are comfortable with aggregated metrics and redacted, non-PII telemetry for quality monitoring.
- Preferred pilot: non-production environment, limited scope (payments flow), then expand after compliance sign-off.

Redwood proposed approach (initial):
- 0-retention flag for 'sensitive' sessions: runtime-only processing, no persistent logging of raw text.
- Short-term ephemeral KV/cache for performance (30 mins) with encryption at rest & in transit.
- Store aggregated metrics (latency, error rates) for 90 days.
- Provide options for Dedicated or Private deployment if required for complete data isolation.

Open items / blockers:
- Legal needs a written exception with exact language and SOW-level commitments (retention windows, deletion certs).
- Procurement questions on SLA, credits, and pricing for custom retention.
- Engineering needs to validate feasibility for 0-retention on hosted environment vs Dedicated/Private.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will share a short draft data-retention-exception doc (attached) for your legal to review.
2) Introduce our security contact for a short technical call (30m) — cc'd Marissa and Rafael.
3) If legal is comfortable, procurement loop to agree SOW + DocuSign.

Would you prefer a technical call tomorrow or early next week?

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | (415) 555-0136

Attachment: 2027-03-25-REDWOOD-DATA-RETENTION-EXCEPTION-DRAFT.pdf (pdf, 4 pages)

From: Sarah Liu <s.liu@fintechcorp.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: security@fintechcorp.com, procurement@fintechcorp.com
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception request / FinTechCorp — follow-up

Thanks Camila — really helpful recap. Confirming a few points from legal and security: 

- Legal will only accept zero retention for raw transcripts that contain PII. That means any session identified as containing PII must not be stored beyond processing.
- Security is OK with aggregated telemetry and redacted logs. They specifically asked that any logs used for debugging remove or mask PII at the edge before transmission.
- For performance reasons, short ephemeral caching (30 minutes) is acceptable as long as data-at-rest is encrypted and we can provide deletion/verifiable retention controls.

Please find attached our security questionnaire (partial) — some fields are placeholders we will complete after the technical call.

We can do a technical call Monday (Mar 29) at 10am PT. Procurement will review SOW after we confirm the retention language.

Sarah Liu
VP Legal & Privacy, FinTechCorp
s.liu@fintechcorp.com

Attachment: FinTechCorp-security-questionnaire-2027.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Data retention exception request / FinTechCorp — follow-up

Looping in Rafael for engineering feasibility. Quick notes from a compliance perspective: 

- 0-retention for PII is feasible but depends on deployment mode. On Hosted: we can implement an on-request 'sensitive' flag that prevents persisting raw text to long-term logs and triggers redaction pipelines; however, it requires a small engineering change and will be scoped as a product configuration (timeline ~2-3 weeks for a prioritized change).
- For absolute guarantee (no writes to disk), Dedicated or Private deployment gives stronger controls and auditability (we can provide deletion certs and KMS controls).
- Edge redaction is recommended: if FinTechCorp can perform client-side redaction or tokenization, that reduces risk. Otherwise we'll implement server-side redaction + PII detection with manual review options.

Action items for us:
- Rafael to confirm the exact implementation effort and whether ephemeral cache can be constrained to memory-only and TTL-based eviction (no disk swap).
- Draft a short SOW clause for zero-retention sessions and proposed retention windows for telemetry.

Rafael — can you take a look and flag any blockers?

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Customer Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <s.liu@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, procurement@fintechcorp.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception request / FinTechCorp — follow-up

Hi Sarah — thanks and appreciated. Following our tech call today (great overview), here is a proposed mutual action plan to move to pilot: 

Mutual action plan (proposed)
- Week 0: Sign pilot SOW with retention language: zero-retention for PII-containing sessions; aggregated metrics retained 90 days; redacted logs retained 24 hours for troubleshooting.
- Week 1: Security/engineering kickoff (Marissa + Rafael) to validate edge redaction and confirm ephemeral cache only (no disk persistence).
- Week 2-4: Pilot in Dedicated dev environment (payments sandbox) with up to 10k requests/day.
- Post-pilot: If satisfactory, draft enterprise SOW for production rollout, include SLA and retention certs.

Commercial notes
- Custom retention and Dedicated environment will carry a small engineering uplift + Dedicated pricing delta. I will put together an updated commercial estimate for procurement once we agree on SOW language.
- For hosted customers, 0-retention is possible but less auditable; recommend Dedicated for full compliance posture.

Next steps for FinTechCorp:
- Approve pilot SOW language (I attached a one-page SOW excerpt in-line in the draft I sent).
- Procurement to share billing/SOW contact (cc'd).

If that works I'll get legal/ops to prepare the pilot SOW and loop in DocuSign.

Best,
Camila
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Liu <s.liu@fintechcorp.com>

Cc: procurement@fintechcorp.com, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception request / FinTechCorp — follow-up

Camila — thank you. We reviewed the proposed mutual action plan internally and FinTechCorp is comfortable moving forward with the pilot under the following binding conditions: 

1) Zero retention of raw transcripts identified as containing PII. Redwood must ensure no persistent storage of PII-containing raw text beyond processing.
2) Redacted logs for troubleshooting are allowed with a 24-hour retention window; logs must be masked at the edge.
3) Aggregated metrics (non-PII) may be retained up to 90 days.
4) If Hosted is used, Redwood must provide a deletion certification and attestations. Prefer Dedicated for production.

Procurement will send a short SOW to Docusign once Redwood sends the final pilot SOW language. Please have legal/ops prepare the SOW and a brief engineering appendix describing the 0-retention implementation.

Procurement contact: procurement@fintechcorp.com

We are good to proceed — please circulate the pilot SOW draft and we'll route for signatures.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
VP Legal & Privacy, FinTechCorp
